utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We were out discussing, anticipating some of the pre-announced problems. So Madam Registrar, could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam and good morning to you. I see the accused are all here. Defence teams are -- the only conspicuous absence is of Stephane Bourgon. Prosecution I see Mr. Thayer on his own. Am I right? Because I can't see behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So good morning, everybody. Are there any preliminaries? Or shall we finish with the witness first? I understand there were some problems with the transcript which have been solved? Let's start with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Haynes has chosen to stand right behind the column.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I did that for the benefit of the witness, not appreciating it would make me blind to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's all right. Go ahead, Mr. Haynes, I will be following you from the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Haynes, by the way, represents Mr. Pandurevic, here and he will be cross-examining you now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Van Duijn. It's some little while since you've been asked questions in English and if I may say so, your English is excellent. So we have to observe the courtesy of making a break between question and answer so that our discourse can be interpreted for those who don't speak English. Okay?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fine by me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: In 1995, you were 24 years of age, that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I turned 25 in May, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes. And you were a platoon commander in Srebrenica and in your command were 34 men?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I call them men but they were very young men, weren't they? Their average age, I think, was 19.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I imagine many of them had not been on any sort of mission before or even left Holland.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, before you went on your tour of duty, did you together with your platoon and other soldiers attend a training course?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Next to the training course for the air mobile unit that we were -- that we were in, we also had a special training course for the mission, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And this special training course for the mission, was that operated by the United Nations rather than the Royal Dutch army?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was operated by the Royal Dutch army.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And it being a training course that was specific to the mission, were you introduced as it were to the history of the creation of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And so I imagine you received training on the special -- on the Security Council's special resolution and the cease-fire agreement?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, was it part of your training that your mission in Srebrenica was to seek to uphold to the letter the Security Council's resolution and the cease-fire agreement?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Within the guidelines that we were given in the rules of engagement, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And I don't want to go through them but under brief headings, that there should be a cease-fire, that the area should be demarcated, that the area should be demilitarised, that paramilitary and military units should leave the area. That was your mission as you understood it, was it?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: When you arrived in Srebrenica, did it strike you that the objectives of your mission were achievable?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was clear to us that it was a very, very difficult mission, because the cease-fire as was stated was more in word than in actual fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So do I understand the position to be this, that you pretty quickly abandoned the objectives of upholding the Security Council's resolution and the cease-fire agreement?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was not the case but we tried to do the best we could with the means we got at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Right. And I pick this phrase carefully. Ultimately, did you find yourself simply monitoring the way each side behaved?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That resembles more or less the way things had gone, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you did little more than that?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We tried what we could.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to move on now, please, to your relations with the population and the military membership of the enclave. It was the people within the enclave that you had the most regular contact with, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You had regular meetings with people outside the enclave, the Serbian military representatives, but you were in daily contact with the population of the enclave and their military personnel?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not into daily contact with the military personnel within the enclave but, yes, in daily contact with the population, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that you developed friendships with the population within the enclave?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Myself, I myself, not personally, no. But there were some friendships, as you could call it, like that, between our personnel and the local population, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Right. And did you yourself develop closer relationships with, as it were, Muslim military personnel than you did with their Serbian counterparts?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had more frequent meetings with the Muslim military personnel, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now I want to ask you about something in particular about relations with the local population. Did it become apparent to you that the personal security of yourself and your soldiers was compromised by the local population and their knowledge of you personally?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really understand what you mean with my personal security.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I understand why you don't understand. It was a thoroughly bad question. I'll start again. Did it become apparent to you that people in the enclave were able to find out not only who you were but where you lived?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You yourself were such a person who had experience of this but you weren't alone, were you?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I heard that in other cases also --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Sorry to be explicit about this within a very few weeks of arriving in Srebrenica, your girlfriend back in Holland received contact from the brother of a local Muslim commander?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And I imagine that was a very unsettling experience for her.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for us all because I didn't know how my address came with that brother of that Muslim commander or with the Muslim commander himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And was there a suspicion that internal mail was being interfered with by the local population?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, there were more suspicions of our information or personal information was also known to local Muslim military commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And I think also there was a case of the main switch board at Bravo Company being connected to by a member of the local population?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. That's what I heard about, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You've been asked one or two questions about this already but I'd like to develop the theme. It became apparent to you during the course of your time there that there were other agencies at work in and around the enclave, didn't it? By which I mean military agencies.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You were asked yesterday about the presence of the British SAS in the enclave. They were not part of your mission, were they?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe they had their own mission but they were put with us on our compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you didn't know whether their objectives were consistent with yours or wholly inconsistent with yours?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I think you also became aware that there were American military personnel operating in the area of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any information about that as well. The only thing that we noticed, that we found some American rations when we did our patrols.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes. But just to complete the picture, in your contact with Serbian military representatives they voiced their concerns to you, didn't they, that there were Americans operating in the area?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that being so clear, clearly stated to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'll leave it there then. One other thing on that particular point, did you feel from time to time that you were not being given access to assistance that you thought was necessary?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And I'll give one particular example. You were concerned, weren't you, about the question of incoming helicopter flights and the supply of arms?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were concerned about movements in the air at that time, and we requested AWACS support which we didn't get.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, I want to move on to something else you've been asked about briefly and again develop this a little more, which is the question of trade with the local population. Was that something that was taking place before you arrived in Srebrenica or was it initiative that developed while you were there?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was already ongoing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I may have misread the impression you gave but I got the impression it's something that you were in favour of.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I saw no harm in it, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: No. You can speak only for your own two observation posts but do I understand the position that trade with the local population was taking place at every observation post?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you could assume that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And was it something that was known to the -- your superior officers, to central command in DutchBat?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think they know -- they knew about it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Was any written guidance given to troops as to the parameters of trade with the local population?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I know of, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Just as an example, it was permissible for members of the battalion to trade with men or women?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it came to goods and I'm not referring to weapons or ammunition or some sort, but if you speak about coffee or bread or possibly doing the laundry, that was permitted, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, not sure you answered the question but I'll ask the next one any way, there was no guidance given as to whether you could trade with only civilians or whether you could trade with the military personnel within the enclave?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you'd anticipated what I'm next going to ask you, which is really what was on offer from the local population? It wasn't just limited to bread and water which you told us about the other day, was it? It was a far wider range of commodities than that.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a little bit more than bread and water but not a very big range of goods.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But it wasn't just goods. Personal services were on offer as well, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, what was the most unusual thing that was ever offered at an operation post?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't -- can't think -- I cannot think of anything that was very unusual because it was a usual trade that was going on. But maybe you have other information that I don't have.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I was looking at the full text of your debriefing, in which I think you suggested that women were offered at observation posts. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard about that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Not at your observation post?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall. I don't have a recollection that it also happened at my observation post, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So far as you're aware was any investigation carried out into that, any guidelines given to soldiers as to how they should respond to such offers?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it was clear that if you were there to help the local population, that you don't go abusing them or using them in any way. So that was clear and I remember that also during briefings, that was again stated that this was not acceptable.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But that's the extent of your knowledge about it, that you heard it happened at other observation posts and people were advised about it?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as I recall now, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can I just deal briefly with the question of arms? You told us that your weaponry degraded, but that wasn't the only problem with weaponry, was it? Weaponry also went missing.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, there was only a machine that was used by the mortar group to calculate coordinates that was missing, and you can say that that was part of the weaponry. It's not a weapon itself but used in the mortar groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can I remind you of something else you said in your debriefing session? Didn't you also tell them that you lost a control unit for a missile launcher?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, this is -- I think you -- there must be something with the translation because I think that we speak about the same thing, but this is a unit that you use to calculate coordinates for mortars and not for missiles.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Right. Thank you very much. Just one last thing about, as it were, life in the enclave and that's about the observation posts themselves. Prior to them being abandoned did anybody observation post, to your knowledge, become inoperative?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean that it was not possible for personnel to stay at that location, that's what I heard from the OPs in the south.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Right. That wasn't really what I meant. What I meant was, was it no longer possible to keep it running because of a shortage of fuel or food or water or electrical supply?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have no knowledge about that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Because just so we get a complete picture of the OPs, each one did have an electrical supply, powered by a generator run by fuel, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Right. Now, I want to move on, please, to the 10th and the 11th of July of 1995. You've told us that you were ordinarily posted in the north east sector and I think in answer to a question from Mr. Zivanovic earlier on, you revealed that your knowledge of the south of the enclave was limited.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But perhaps you can help assist with this. One of the features of the south of the enclave which you will have observed is that it's much more hilly than the north of the enclave, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: The road out of Srebrenica to the south goes steeply uphill and ahead of you lie quite a number of hills?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Before you went to the south of the city on the morning of the 10th of July, had you attended any meeting about what your role should be that morning?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was briefed by Captain Groen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And was this a meeting attended only by members of the battalion or were members of the Muslim forces present too?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was a meeting in the compound of Bravo Company. The headquarters of Captain Groen. And there was only a meeting between him, me and other platoon commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: When you took up your first blocking position, it would be right, wouldn't it, that the Muslim positions were very, very proximate to you?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Literally a few yards away or a few metres away? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Indeed, they remained there so that they could train an RPG on your unit to make you stay?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, your unit consisted of one APC, yourself and five other men?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And might sound a foolish question but an APC is about the size of a delivery van, really, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a little bit bigger than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But it's a single vehicle?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. It's a single --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And during the course of the morning of the 10th of July, did your men remain within the vehicle or did they deploy themselves outside?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first I deployed them also outside, but because of the constant shelling, I chose to get them into the APC because of the shrapnel threat.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Right. Now, I want to explore with you just briefly, as it were, the rules of your engagement. Would I be right to assert that you were only permitted to fire on other forces when you were fired on directly?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You were not permitted to fire on other forces as it were in defence of the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you certainly weren't allowed to fire on other forces in defence of Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no distinction between civilian population and Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: That's very helpful. Now, as has been underlined previously, you've given a number of statements, debriefings and accounts and evidence on this topic, and one of the things that you've never mentioned is the question of incoming small arms fire. Can we take it that at no stage prior to the appearance of Serbian forces later that morning were you the recipient of incoming small-arms fire?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not during the stage of the blocking position, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The shells that were -- that you've referred to and that were landing, they were all large-bore shells, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Picking up something you said previously, they were all the sort of shells that were being fired from a distance of 10 to 15 kilometres away?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my impression, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes. And in terms of the number of shells that landed near your position, there were two early in the morning and a few later on?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There must have been more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, it may well be I have to take you something you said previously but I want to you think about that. Two shells early in the morning and a few later on.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that refers to the shells that were falling or hitting very close to my APC.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm going to invite you to consider one other statement. You never believed, did you, that the shells that landed near you were aimed at you?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated before that it is difficult when you shoot a shell from that distance on, it is very hard to aim directly at one point, but that it was aimed at our general location. That was clear because otherwise they wouldn't have fallen there. But I cannot have the idea that it was aimed directly at my APC or at other APCs of the UN.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you again. That's very, very helpful. So whilst you were sitting there, you didn't believe that you had been fired upon directly either by small weaponry or by artillery?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, if you are being shelled by artillery, it doesn't matter if they aim directly at you. If the shells fall within 50 metres or yards, as you say, of your APC, it's time to get out of there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: That again is very helpful. Because there came a point, didn't there, when you could see Bosnian Serb infantry coming over a hill ahead of you?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And as you say, there comes a moment when it's time to get out of there. That is not what you did, though, is it?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I waited until I got the assignment to withdraw, and I waited until that was the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, that's not quite what you did. When you saw the Bosnian Serb infantry come over the hill ahead of you, you instructed your gunner to fire at them?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You gave him that order. Who gave you that order?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Being into constant contact through the radio, we had the assignment that if the Serb forces would stay advancing, we would first shoot over head, if we could see them, and then shoot directly at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm sure you're -- that's very helpful but who was it who told you to fire?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was Captain Groen, over the radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And I think it's the position, isn't it, that your gunner continued to fire at Serbian troops until you could see them no more?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was difficult for me to see the Serbian troops themselves later on but he assured me that he couldn't see them any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Right. Was that because they had retreated or because he had killed them?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. We didn't check.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Didn't you ask him?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, at the same time that you were firing at Serbian troops, the Muslim forces around you were also firing, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe at that stage they were not in the vicinity of my APC firing south. I think at that stage, there was only one or two Muslim fighters with an RPG aiming at our APC.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Right. I'm going to quote something that you said in the Blagojevic case and see if you can help me with it and then I have to put something specifically to you. It's at page 1052 and it's lines 3 to 8. You were asked, where did you see the Muslim soldiers? And you said, "Near to my location." And you were asked, "Okay. What were they doing?" And you said, "They were shooting in the direction of the south. It wasn't clear to me at what they were shooting or they were shooting or they were moving forwards towards the south and back again -- or back again." Now, that is at a point during the course of the morning of the 10th of July you're describing. Was there a point in the course of the morning of the 10th of July when the Muslim forces moved forwards towards the south?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no specific action towards the south of them. As I described before, there were sometimes moving towards the south and then withdrawing again and we could see the same fighters going in the direction of the south and coming back again.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Right. In military terms, did it appear to you that something of a counteroffensive went on during the course of the morning?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not a -- not a counteroffensive as I would describe it, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But fighters moving forward, forwards towards where the fire was coming from and then coming back again?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I just want to complete the picture of, as it were, you giving the order to fire. Did you tell us that you were there alone in your APC and there were two or three Muslim fighters training an RPG on you at that time; other than that, there were no other forces?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that was the case. I was of course not alone in my APC but together with my personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm going to leave that now and move on for just a few minutes to Potocari and I've not got very many questions to ask you about that because you've been asked a lot of them. The man Captain Mane, can we take it that all the information you had about him you got from him?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, through his interpreter, Miki, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you didn't seek to check anything that he told you about himself?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Frankly, there was no time or reason to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And over the course of two days, he was pretty central to what was going on at Potocari?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was the one in charge at that location, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And he dealt with not just you but a number of refugees as well? He spoke to them.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have a recollection of that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of him directly speaking to refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Last few questions: In answer to a question from Madam Fauveau yesterday, it might not have been Madam Fauveau. I'm sorry, it was at page 40, lines 9 to 11, you were asked about, as it were, the number of men that were present amongst the group at Potocari and you said, "When you look at the total number of men that I saw, and the men that I saw singled out, that must resemble more than 300 or 350 men." The question I ask you to follow on from that is, when you say that you saw more than 300, 350 men singled out, that is the number that you saw actually taken, not the number you saw taken away before your intervention?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is the total estimation of the number of men being singled out during the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I'm interested about that because Madam Fauveau did establish with you yesterday that the number you saw in the house on the first day was between I think you said 15 and 50. Yes?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And the number you saw in the "White House" on the second day was between 50 and 100, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So in effect the number of men you saw placed in those two houses over the course of two days was a maximum of 150?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The men I saw at that stage resemble more or less the figure of 150 but when I look at the two days, the whole days, thinking and making an estimation of the men that were singled out, it resembles a higher number but I was not there at the "White House" the second day the whole time and I don't know if there were earlier transports before my arrival there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes. I would just like to finish this with a general question. In the years following your service in Srebrenica, you came under some criticism, didn't you, from some of your colleagues for what you did there?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And it was your belief that your role in the evacuation of the refugees had hampered your career in the following years?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not my belief. At first it was my belief but also in the parliamentary inquiry it became clear in the early years after the fall of the enclave that was indeed the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But just to be clear, you're sure you did the right thing there, you did what people wanted you to do, and it was the only choice and the best one in their interests?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure I did the right thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Assisting with the evacuation?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Assisting the refugees, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Haynes. Is there re-examination, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, there is. Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead. Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning, Major.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yesterday you answered a question posed by my learned colleague Ms. Fauveau that you were indeed able to take leave during your stay in Bosnia. I'm afraid I don't have the cite to the transcript because we didn't have that available because of the glitch this morning. But I believe you did answer that you were indeed able to take leave and to return to the enclave. Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall when you were permitted to take that leave and re-enter?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in the early stages of the mission. I believe it was in the end of February, March.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, at some point, was there a change in the ability of DutchBat personnel to take leave and subsequently to reenter the enclave, Major?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the fact, and even that transport had been postponed and it was not clear if it would go through but from March on, there were a lot of difficulties getting people that went on leave back into the enclave, which led to considerable amount of personnel of DutchBat staying in the Netherlands and they were not able to come back to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, do you recall also being asked yesterday by Madam Fauveau about your October 25th, 1995 statement to the Office of the Prosecutor regarding the number of men whom you observed in front of the house that you described with no facade, and that was just referred to again by my learned colleague, Mr. Haynes in his examination. Do you remember those questions, sir?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you've also been referred by various of my colleagues to your Dutch army debriefing statement at Assen that was taken on the 12th and 13th of 1995, September 1995, about a month and a half before you gave your statement to the OTP. Do you remember being asked various questions about that Assen debriefing, sir?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, do you recall whether during that Assen debriefing discussing how many men you recalled seeing in front of the house with no facade on 12 July?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall as you sit here today what your answer was or what the number was that you stated to the debriefers in Assen about how many men you recalled seeing in front of the house with no facade?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the exact number which I stated there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would seeing a copy of that report refresh your recollection, sir, about what you said at that time?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour, it's been previously marked as Defence Exhibit 7 D0055, and if I -- with the assistance of Madam Usher, because I don't think it's been placed into the e-court system yet, show the witness page 14 of the English and it's page 9 of the B/C/S translation and I would just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need to have it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we could place it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just call your attention to the first, the top highlighted section in orange and just ask you to read that and I'd ask you if that refreshes your recollection about what you stated to the debriefers in Assen?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will read the first part and I quote, "the whole day of the -- the whole of the first day, the men remained in the house open facade, without windows. He thought 50 men in total."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And does that jog your memory, sir, as to whether it was 50 or 15 to 50?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember stating that and I recognise this as a part of my statement there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. Do you also recall being asked some questions by my learned colleague Mr. Lazarevic yesterday and that would be from page 41 line 10 through page 42 line 23, also about your October 25th 1995 OTP statement, about seeing passports and other personal property near the bus station versus near the "White House"? Do you recall that line of questioning, sir?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall whether in that same Assen debriefing that we just discussed, discussing seeing passports in front of the "White House" at that time? Do you recall whether or not you did that, sir?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that I stated there that I saw passports in front of the "White House."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, do you recall being asked also by Mr. Lazarevic at page 51, line 15 through page 53 line 24, about your testimony before the Dutch government where he read the following testimony and I'll just read it again rather than referring to the transcript pages. The question was: "You tackled the Serbian commander about this matter. What was his reaction?" The answer: "I asked him what he was going to do with the Muslim men. He gave me the same story that they intended interrogating them to find out whether there were any war criminals amongst them. Then I put it to him that if there are no passports men could give false names and that the story about checking the identities was no longer valid. He just laughed as if to say what are you getting so excited about, they don't need their passports any more. Other than that, he didn't give me any further explanation." Now, do you remember that line of questioning from yesterday, sir?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall as you sit here the questions and answers you gave when you were asked about this same conversation during your testimony in 2000 in the Krstic case?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the exact phrasing, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to read you the relevant questions and your answers from the Krstic testimony, if I may just read it in rather than placing it on the ELMO, Mr. President. This is from the Krstic trial transcript page 1768, line 22. Question: "Did you see anything else at the 'White House' apart from these men that were packed inside and outside the 'White House'?" Answer: "When I came up to the 'White House,' and as you can see in front of the 'White House' there is a large lawn, it was covered totally with personal belongings, with pictures, holiday snapshots as well as passports and others identity papers." Question: "Now, after you'd seen this did you speak to anybody about what you'd seen at the 'White House'?" Answer: "I spoke to Mane again because the first day of the deportations, when I noticed that the men were singled out, I asked him why, and he gave me the explanation of them wanting to distinguish who was a war criminal and who was not. So I asked him again because I saw all the passports and identity papers why they couldn't take them with them, because that was in front of the house and not on the men itself. He said, well, they don't need the stuff that's there. They don't need it any more. Then I asked him how he could explain the fact that if they wanted to know who was a war criminal and who was not, they could do that without identity papers because if they would give a false name, it wouldn't be on the list of war criminals and the person would go free and join the rest of the convoy to Tuzla. Then he more or less laughed at me and said, 'Well, don't make such a fuss out of it. They just don't need their passports any more.'" Do you recall giving that testimony, sir, in Krstic in 2000?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Major. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Thayer. I understand there may be some questions from the Bench. Judge Kwon. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I have a brief question. Can the witness be shown map 6 or ERN number 05050371. Major Van Duijn, not being a military man myself, I'm more familiar with the simple maps than with a detailed military maps. Can you see the map?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your base was at UN base in Potocari or Charlie, not the Bravo Company in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's correct, sir. My base was the most northerly base near Potocari.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But I heard that you had a briefing at Bravo Company, this morning, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the morning, I went over to the Bravo Company to take the blocking positions. I went from the UN base in Potocari to the UN base from Bravo Company, and that's where I was briefed by Captain Groen and there he gave me the orders about the -- about the blocking positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you mark the -- your blocking position in this map?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My blocking position was Bravo 3 and was just located in the outskirts, the southern outskirts of the town. This is the wrong location. The pen doesn't work quite correctly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Do you want to cancel that --

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because it was not on the good location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How can he cancel it? Madam Registrar? Okay. That's it. All done. So.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try it again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's too southern but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's do it this way. Can we zoom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We can zoom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we can zoom and then we could zoom into the bottom half of the map. Yes. Stop there. Now, perhaps he can -- does it help you better now?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's just that the pen is not corresponding to the place where I put it. This is more correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You once mentioned the position point 2. It is intersection of the roads which -- the roads which lead one leading from Potocari to Srebrenica and the one to Susnjari, was that right.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And if you could briefly tell me the direction VRS force advanced.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The direction --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In this map, yes.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The direction the VRS force advanced was using the road in a northern direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you not mention two directions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I was at the point a little bit north of point 02, and if I can help with that to mark it on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. This is point 02. So during the 11th, we basically drew back from the blocking positions, back through the town of Srebrenica, the compound of UN Bravo Company, back to point 02, and the Serb forces then were advancing from the south and shelling also from the south. When the next day the morning of the 12th, my position was just a little bit north of point 02, then the VRS forces that I saw advancing came from the north. They came on the eastern side of the UN base and then came on the road at point 02 and then came north to the location where I was. If you look at the schematic map now, the UN base is just a little bit too close to point 02 and has to be put up a little bit more to the north to be correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could mark an arrow there, the direction VRS advanced from the north on this map.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And also using the road that was the other direction they came from, from the north.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That helps my understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. One moment, before we are done with this. The -- for the record, the witness has put two arrows on this map. One is at 20 minutes from observation post golf. Why -- yeah, okay. That according to him signifies the direction of the first attack or approach of the VRS. And then he put a second arrow pointing from the words, "UN base" towards the red circle which is at 3.00 of the words, "PTO 2" which the witness himself wrote on the map. That is indicative of, according to him, the direction of the attack or approach of the VRS on the second occasion. Yesterday, however, you indicated two, when you were referring to the approach of the VRS, near 02, you put -- you placed two arrows. Could you also put on the map the other arrow? If it is possible.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, of course. The other arrow was following the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That road.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Now the witness has put another -- a third arrow at 35 minutes from observation post P, Papa. Okay. Any further questions, Judge Stole? Judge? Major, we have come to the end of your testimony. Please sign the map that you've worked with now.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And that will be introduced in the records as one of the Court documents, in-court documents. All right. Major we have come to the ends of your testimony. I thank you very much for having come over to give evidence. I thank you on my own behalf, I thank you on behalf of my colleagues, Judge Kwon from Korea, Judge Prost from Canada, and Judge Stole from Norway and I thank you also on behalf of the Tribunal in general. You'll receive now all the assistance you require to facilitate your return to your duties or home or whatever. Since I assume you would be going back to Vicenza in Italy, on behalf of everyone here I also wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, I understand there may be some slight business to transact. First of course will be the admission of -- tendering and admission of exhibits. Let's start with you, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President the Prosecution has three exhibits to tender through Major Van Duijn's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thought it was four.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We have four. It's the cleared version that's -- we can offer that. I understand that has been subject to some dispute but I would offer it again. It's P01516, the aerial of Potocari.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's start with that one R there any objections? Yes, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Although we didn't cross this witness I thought we understood with the aerial photographs we are going to have that all stayed for the moment and I just want to reserve our objection to that and the introduction of that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. Ostojic, that's how it's going to be. Let's proceed with the next and then we'll tell you what our decision is. Next?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The next is PIC 00009. That is the same aerial of Potocari marked by the witness where he has indicated the DutchBat compound and the refugee area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Any objections on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Same objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Next?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The next is PIC 00011, same aerial of Potocari marked by the witness indicating the lawn area.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Same objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I wonder what one of your colleagues is going to say who made use of the same aerial images and had the witness mark them, put marks on them. But let's come to that later. Yes, next document you wish to tender, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The final exhibit is PIC 00012, the same aerial marked by the witness indicating the "White House."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, we will be deciding the question of exhibits -- you made use of this same aerial image of Potocari, and the witness has put on that image also some markings. And my understanding, correct me if I'm wrong, is that you also wish to tender that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You stand by that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We did it as a PO 1516.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And do you object to that, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may address the Court I don't think it's as complicated as it might seem at first blush. Quite candidly if the Prosecution introduces an exhibit with the witness it's not our obligation to foresee that the Court will accept or deny that exhibit into evidence. It's our duty to examine the witness with that exhibit whether the Court accepts or not it was the evidence and simply my objection is to preserve our prior objections to these aerial photographs consistent with what I thought was the Court's ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's my objection to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So I think the position should emerge clear now. As far as P 01516 itself, unmarked, in et cetera original state is concerned, that has already been marked for identification on a previous occasion and it will remain so marked rather than admitted, of course, pending the resolution of the various issue that is have been raised in relation to all aerial images. As regards PIC in court, in other words, 0009 to 12, those will be admitted because they have been simply been made use of in the course of the testimony, and marked by the witness. The same will apply to the one being submitted by the Defence of Mr. Popovic, with the understanding that it is not the tendering of P01516 that is being sought by the Defence of Mr. Popovic, but the -- what would be in-court number -- I wouldn't know what number this will be given. It will be 1 DIC 13. All right?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: To that disposes of your requests, Mr. Thayer, and yours. And what remains to be seen is the documents tendered by the Borovcanin Defence team. Let's start with the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The first one is a copy of a map. The reference is R 0132155, to 156, included with the OTP proofing of the witness of the 14 September 2006. This contains also some markings made by the witness himself. It has a 65 ter number 4 DIC 00014. Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: None, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So it is so admitted. Next is excerpt of video 3914, counter reading from 19 minutes point 34 to 19 minutes point 50 and 21 minutes point 10 seconds to 21 minutes point 16 seconds. It has Prosecution 65 ter marking which is 2007. Is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So it is being admitted. Now, we had agreed on the system to be adopted when it is a -- Prosecution. So it will be -- yes. It will be marked as 4 -- as 4D exhibit with, immediately afterwards, the Prosecution 65 ter number. Now comes the crux of the discussion. Borovcanin team seeks admission of the OTP witness statement of the 25th of October 1995, not of the entire statement but of two segments thereof. One is -- relates to paragraph 8, page 8 of the English version, with the corresponding paragraph 7 of page 7 of the B/C/S version. Is there any objection on the part of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can I clarify one thing? The Defence is minded to certain part of the whole witness statement. The consequence of it, the remaining part will be deleted from the system or the whole statement will remain to understand the context? What's the position of this in relation to this? I'd like to hear from the Defence and the Prosecution as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And also, if I may add, Judge Kwon, the question of -- it is my understanding that this paragraph was read out in English, translated into B/C/S. At the same time there was a translation copy available on the screen for the accused to be able to follow at the time So there is also the issue of whether you really need to have this excerpt tendered as an exhibit or whether you are happy to co-exist with the transcript of the proceedings. That's another issue that you may -- maybe you wish to consider, both of you, both you, Mr. Lazarevic, and Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you for drawing my attention to this. Actual little we made use only of this part of the statement in cross-examination in the witness and you're absolutely right when saying that it's already contained in the transcript so actually we don't need any admission of the statement of this witness at all. So we would like to delete this from your witness -- from our document -- evidence list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That relieves my concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. So for the record, the Prosecution -- the Defence team for accused Borovcanin does not seek any further introduction of the excerpt from 4 D00036. And that is without prejudice for any further seeking to introduce the entire statement or parts thereof at a later stage in another context. So I think that is perfectly clear. Then there is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Same applies to our evidence number 4 because it's same principle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Same applies to the next entry; that is, to be specific, in case there has been a reference already to the excerpt to wit paragraph 4 from page 27 in the English version, paragraph 8 from page 22 of the Serbo-Croat version of 4 D00038. Therefore, this is not being sought for the time being, without prejudice, as explained earlier. Then there is the witness's statement again from the same document, another excerpt, paragraph 5, page 24 of the English version, paragraph 2 on page 20 of the Serbo-Croat version. I take it that you take the same position? So both excerpts from the same document. Thank you. And then there is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- finally, I think, the excerpt from the Srebrenica trial video from counter reading 2 hours 24 minutes 51 seconds through 2 hours 24 minutes 55 seconds, dated 13th July 1995, which is part of video 4458 with Prosecution 65 ter number PO 2047. All right. The advice we are receiving is that this video has already been made use of by the Prosecution so there is no further need for it to be tendered again by anyone else. Do you accept that, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I have no notice from any other Defence team of an intention to introduce any other documents, exhibits, all right. Thank you. I just want to make sure, Madam Registrar, that the transcript problem that you told me about has been fixed.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, they are working on that. I don't know if it's already solved but it will be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But if there are problems relating to it that trouble you, please come forward and let us know. Can we go into private session for a couple of minutes, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that concludes the sitting for the day. We will reconvene 16th of -- I think it's in the morning. I thank you so much. And see you soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 16th day of October, 2006, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 10.37 a.m.,
